11	## General guidelines
12	
13	- Read existing code before modifying it. Understand the patterns already in use.
14	- Keep changes minimal and focused — fix what was asked, nothing more.
15	- Do not add speculative features, premature abstractions, or unused helpers.
16	- Prefer editing existing files over creating new ones.
17	- Never commit secrets, credentials, or .env files.
18	
19	## Workstation layout
20	
21	Repo locations are host-specific — match the convention of the machine you're on
22	(on Windows, check `$env:COMPUTERNAME`).
23	
24	- **`ZENDA`** (Windows): local clones live under `D:\repos\<github-owner-or-org>\<repo>`
25	  (for example `D:\repos\adam-s-daniel\wsl-automation`). Clone new repos there, and
26	  assume existing repos live there rather than under the user profile
27	  (`C:\Users\<user>\...`).
28	
29	## Code quality
30	
31	- Follow the idioms and style already established in this repo.
32	- Write code that is clear enough to not need comments; add comments only when intent is non-obvious.
33	- Avoid introducing new dependencies unless strictly necessary.
34	- Every public interface change should include corresponding test updates.
35	
36	## Security
37	
38	- Validate all external input (user input, API responses, file contents).
39	- Never construct SQL, shell commands, or HTML by string concatenation with untrusted data.
40	- Use parameterized queries, shell arrays, and context-aware escaping respectively.
41	- Do not disable TLS verification, authentication, or CSRF protection.
42	
43	## Data exposure in CI and public repos
44	
45	Treat CI run logs, job summaries, artifacts, workflow run pages, and git history
46	as **public** on a public repo. (Real incident: a workflow printed the owner's
47	email addresses and their correspondents' into a public Actions log.)
48	
49	- **Never print personal or sensitive data to a log** — no emails, contacts,
50	  names, IDs, mailbox sizes/counts, tokens, or anything "useful to an attacker or
51	  scammer." Deliver sensitive results out-of-band (e.g. email the account itself,
52	  write to a private store) and log only a non-identifying status line.
53	- **Don't interpolate `${{ inputs.* }}` / `${{ github.event.* }}` into a `run:`
54	  block** — the rendered command is echoed to the log. Read inputs from
55	  `$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` inside the script and `::add-mask::` sensitive values
56	  before use. `::add-mask::` only scrubs the log *stream*, not other surfaces.
57	- **Put sensitive config in secrets, not plaintext inputs or `vars`.** Only
58	  secret *values* are masked in logs.
59	- **Sanitize error output** — never dump an API/HTTP response body on failure (it
60	  can quote personal data); reduce it to a status code + machine error type, and
61	  keep the data-bearing serialization/call inside the try/catch.
62	- **Least privilege:** set `permissions:` to the minimum (usually
63	  `contents: read`) and require approval for outside-collaborator fork PRs.
64	- **Test fixtures use reserved `example.com` / `example.net` domains only** —
65	  never a real address; fixtures get committed and logged.
66	
67	### git history & metadata
68	- **Sanitize before the first commit.** Fixing the current file does not remove
69	  data from history. If sensitive data was committed, rewrite history to drop the
70	  commits, delete every ref that points at them (branches, tags, **PRs**), and
71	  force-push. GitHub garbage-collects unreachable objects on its own schedule
72	  (days to weeks) — until then they remain reachable *by SHA* — and you can ask
73	  GitHub Support to expedite for a public repo. (This is the deliberate exception
74	  to "don't force-push"; it is a security remediation.)
75	- **Commit with the GitHub `…@users.noreply.github.com` identity** on public
76	  repos so a real email is not baked into commit author/committer metadata.
77	
78	## Automation vs branch protection
79	
80	Fleet repos enforce PR-only default branches via ruleset, managed as code in
81	`repo-settings` (see its ADR 0001). Design automation accordingly:
82	
83	- Never design a bot that pushes to a protected default branch ad hoc — the
84	  push is rejected (GH013), even from the repo's own workflows.
85	- Generated data (badges, run summaries, reports, dashboards) belongs on a
86	  dedicated unprotected results branch (e.g. skills-evals' `eval-results`);
87	  consumers read from that branch and treat its content as untrusted.
88	- The rare bot that genuinely must write to a default branch needs a ruleset
89	  bypass actor declared in repo-settings' `fleet.yml` — never a hand-granted
90	  UI bypass (the drift report flags those). The AGENTS.md sync App is the
91	  standing example.
92	- PR + auto-merge is not a sanctioned bot-write path for fleet repos; the
93	  cms-platform-managed repos (outside the fleet ruleset) use it by their own
94	  design.
95	
96	## Testing
97	
98	- Run the existing test suite before considering a task complete.
99	- New behavior requires new tests; bug fixes require regression tests.
100	- Tests should be deterministic — no sleeping, no network calls, no reliance on wall-clock time.
101	
102	## Subagent delegation (model routing)
103	
104	- Don't write code in the main loop: run the implementation in a subagent on an
105	  appropriately lower-power model (e.g. the Agent tool's `model` override in
106	  Claude Code; skip if the harness has no subagent support).
107	- Route by mechanicalness: smallest model (haiku-class) for exactly-specified
108	  edits — pin bumps, renames, config/doc tweaks; mid-tier (sonnet-class) for
109	  normal implementation from a clear spec.
110	- The main loop keeps root-cause investigation, architectural decisions,
111	  writing the spec, and review of the subagent's diff before commit.
112	- Escalate the model rather than ship a wrong diff when the task is genuinely
113	  subtle (cross-repo invariants, race conditions).
114	- Don't assume the subagent sees this file: general-purpose and custom
115	  subagents receive the full memory hierarchy (imports included), but
116	  Explore/Plan-type agents and SDK harnesses with `settingSources: []` skip
117	  repo guidance entirely. Restate load-bearing constraints (style, test
118	  command, invariants) in the delegation prompt, and don't hand
119	  guidance-sensitive work to agents that won't see it.
120	- Give the subagent a precise spec — files, exact changes, house style, the
121	  test command to run. Subagent output is gated by the same test/CI proof as
122	  any other change.
123	
124	## Skills ecosystem
125	
126	- The canonical skills registry is `github.com/Adam-S-Daniel/agentskills`,
127	  organized as three bundle plugins — `adam` (general-purpose, cloud-safe;
128	  default-on), `adam-local` (machine-bound), and `fastmail` — each holding
129	  `skills/<skill>/` directories.
130	- In Claude Code with the marketplace installed, invoke a skill as
131	  `/adam:<skill>` (e.g. `/adam:pin-actions-to-sha`).
132	- Local machines get the marketplace plus per-agent symlinks via that repo's
133	  `setup.sh`.
134	- Cloud sessions currently get **no** plugins from repo-declared settings — a
135	  known Claude Code limitation (see agentskills' `docs/decisions/0001`) — so
136	  don't assume bundle skills are available there.
137	- New reusable skills graduate **into** the registry (sensitive ones into
138	  `agentskills-private`) rather than living on in a consumer repo.
139	
140	## Git practices
141	
142	- Write concise commit messages that explain *why*, not just *what*.
143	- One logical change per commit.
144	- Do not amend published commits or force-push shared branches.

209	
210	## Code style
211	
212	- Python 3.12+. No type stubs or mypy. Use type hints where they aid readability.
213	- Dollar amounts in results.md: round to nearest penny (`.2f`).
214	- Durations in results.md: always in minutes with 1 decimal (`{seconds/60:.1f}min`).
215	- No emojis in code or docs unless the user asks.
216	
217	## Terminology
218	
219	When the runtime wrapper uses `language_mode` (Python-side variable name), the
220	*user-facing* axis is called **language**, never "mode". This covers docs,
221	prompts, report prose, and LLM summaries. The internal field name stays
222	`language_mode` so existing metrics.json readers don't break; everything else
223	says "language" (e.g. "default/Python, bash, powershell, typescript-bun").
224	Historical runs also carry a `powershell-tool` language, but reports collapse
225	it into `powershell` at display time (`_disp_mode`, #30) — the raw
226	`language_mode` and on-disk `powershell-tool-*` cell dirs are preserved.
227	Rationale: "mode" is ambiguous with agent-approval-modes and execution modes;
228	"language" is the concept readers expect.
229	
230	## Repository rules
231	
232	- **No agent-generated `.github/workflows/` at repo root.** Agent workflows only exist inside workspaces under `workspaces/`. The repo's own CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) is the exception.
233	- **Never fix agent-generated code.** The benchmark measures autonomous output. Do not manually fix, edit, or patch workflow files in `workspaces/` or `results/*/generated-code/`.
234	- **`runner.py` observes and records, never intervenes** on agent code or errors.
235	- **Workspaces are throwaway.** Don't commit `workspaces/` contents.
236	- **`results/` is committed.** It contains archived metrics, generated code, and transcripts.
237	- **`CLAUDE.md` is only a pointer.** All instructions go in `AGENTS.md`. Never put substantive content in `CLAUDE.md` — it should only reference this file.
238	- **Always set effort AND context explicitly on every run.** Pass `--effort` for every effort-capable model (i.e. everything but Haiku 4.5) and select an explicit context variant (`opus47-1m` vs `opus47-200k`, etc.). Never rely on the CLI defaults: the default effort is version-dependent (it flipped `medium`→`high` at CC 2.1.117) AND is not recorded in `metrics.json`, so cells run without `--effort` cannot be labeled with certainty afterwards. `runner.py` logs a prominent WARNING (not a refusal) when `--effort` is unset for an effort-capable model.
239	  - **We are NOT studying "default/no-effort" behavior as a condition.** We don't care about "what do you get when you don't specify effort." A run that omitted `--effort` is labeled purely by the effort it *actually* used (derived from the CC-version default) — e.g. the historical no-`--effort` base Sonnet 5 run is `sonnet5-1m-high` because it ran at the CC default `high`, and it is treated identically to an explicit-`high` run. Do NOT add a `default`/`no-effort` label, an inline "derived" marker, or otherwise try to keep no-effort runs distinct; and do not spin up new no-effort runs to characterize default behavior. (The derived-effort inference itself is documented in each combined report's "Model label conventions" section.)
240	- **Standard language set is `default,powershell,bash,typescript-bun` (4 modes).** Drop `powershell-tool`: under WSL it is functionally identical to `powershell` (same prompt body, same pwsh), so it adds a redundant cell per task without a distinct signal.
241	- **Post a live status heartbeat during runs.** Roughly every 30 minutes while a run is in flight, relay the full `python3 monitor.py --total <N>` report (run-health + structural metrics + head-to-head) so progress, pace/ETA, and any emerging failures are visible without waiting for completion.
242	
243	## Running on Claude Code on the web
244	
245	The benchmark can run inside a Claude Code on the web cloud session instead of a
246	laptop/WSL box. `./run-benchmark-web.sh [--setup-only] [runner.py args...]`
247	provisions the sandbox and hands off to `runner.py`; it is idempotent, so
248	re-running after a session restart only fixes what is missing.
249	
250	What is different from a laptop, and how each difference is handled:
251	
252	| Difference | Handling |
253	|---|---|
254	| Docker CLI present, **daemon not running** (no init system) — `act` and every v3+ task fail | `run-benchmark-web.sh` starts `dockerd` and waits for the socket |
255	| Session runs as **root**, and `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` refuses to start as root | `cell_env()` sets `IS_SANDBOX=1`. The sandbox already exports `IS_SANDBOX=yes`, which the CLI does **not** honour — only `"1"` works, so the value is forced, not defaulted |
256	| All egress goes through a **TLS-terminating proxy**; containers trust neither its CA nor reach its 127.0.0.1 address | act's runner image is built on a base that installs the proxy CA; `~/.config/act/actrc` adds `--network host` plus the proxy env |
257	| That proxy answers **plain HTTP with 405** | The CA base layer rewrites every apt source to `https://`, and the image build passes `https_proxy` only (never `http_proxy`) |
258	| `api.github.com` is **blocked** by egress policy, so "latest release" installers fail | actionlint/shellcheck/act are pinned to exact release URLs at the top of the script |
259	| act ≥ 0.2.8x **force-pulls** the runner image, which exists only locally | `--pull=false` in `~/.config/act/actrc` |
260	| pwsh, Pester, act, actionlint, shellcheck, bats absent (node and bun are present) | installed by the script; pwsh comes from the Microsoft apt repo for the sandbox's own Ubuntu version |
261	| runner.py is launched **from inside a Claude Code session**, so cells would inherit the parent's session env | `cell_env()` scrubs `INHERITED_SESSION_ENV_VARS` before each cell |
262	| Sessions are **ephemeral** (reclaimed after inactivity) | `runner.py` already commits+pushes `results/` per completed cell; resume with `--resume <run-dir>` |
263	
264	The env scrub is load-bearing, not hygiene. An inherited `CLAUDE_EFFORT` /
265	`MAX_THINKING_TOKENS` overrides the cell's own effort, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`
266	stamps every cell with the parent's session id, `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH`
267	caps the cell's subagents, and the nested-session markers change the CLI's tool
268	surface (measured: 40 tools unscrubbed vs 30 scrubbed).
269	
270	### What still does not work in a cloud session
271	
272	Two post-run steps are blocked by the sandbox's egress policy, not by the
273	harness. Both are laptop-only for now; do not try to route around the policy.
274	
275	- **`version_docs.py`** builds each run's `claude-code-<version>.md` from a
276	  tree listing at `api.github.com`, which the policy answers with 403 (the
277	  `raw.githubusercontent.com` changelog fetch works fine). A cloud run's
278	  results.md will link a per-version doc that does not exist until someone
279	  regenerates from a laptop.
280	- **The Gemini half of the judge panel.** `test_quality.py --llm-judge
281	  --deliverable-judge` works with `--judges haiku45` (the `claude-cli`
282	  provider), but the `agy` CLI behind `gemini31pro` is not installed in the
283	  sandbox and `gemini-api` needs `GEMINI_API_KEY`. Score a cloud run with the
284	  single-judge form, or run the panel later from a laptop.
285	
286	### Comparability caveats — do not pool cloud and laptop cells blindly
287	
288	`system_info.execution_environment` (`claude-code-web` vs `local`) is recorded in
289	every run manifest, and each cell's `session.tools_available` now records the
290	tool-surface *names* (not just the count). Before comparing a cloud run against a
291	laptop baseline, check both:
292	
293	- **Tool surface.** Cloud cells run under the deferred-tool regime — `Glob`,
294	  `Grep` and `TodoWrite` are behind `ToolSearch`, and cloud-only tools
295	  (`Workflow`, `Task*`, `Cron*`, `SendUserFile`, …) are offered instead. That is
296	  a different agent, not just a different machine.
297	- **Machine size.** 4 CPUs / 15 GB and a shared writable disk allowance, versus
298	  whatever the laptop had. Durations are not comparable; `act` container startup
299	  in particular is disk-bound.
300	- **Cost/wall-clock.** Unchanged per cell, but a cloud session is reclaimed after
301	  inactivity, so long campaigns need the resume loop rather than one long run.
302	
303	Use cloud runs to compare *within* a cloud campaign (language A vs language B,
304	model A vs model B), and treat cross-environment deltas as unvalidated.
305	
306	## Architecture
307	
308	### Key files
309	
310	- `models.py` — single source of truth for model IDs and token pricing. Update here when Anthropic changes prices.
311	- `runner.py` — benchmark harness. Runs agents via `claude -p`, collects metrics, pushes results. Imports from `models.py` and `generate_results.py`. Robustness invariants added 2026-06:
312	  - **Single-runner lock.** On startup it takes an exclusive non-blocking `flock` on `<repo>/.runner.lock` (`acquire_single_runner_lock`); a second runner exits(2) rather than execute cells concurrently — concurrent cells compete for CPU/Docker/pwsh and confound each other's timing/cost. (Released automatically on exit.)
313	  - **Resume validity.** `--resume` skips a cell only when its `metrics.json` is non-empty + parseable (`_metrics_valid`), so a write interrupted by a crash/teardown is re-run rather than skipped forever, leaving a hole.
314	  - **Honest push logging + commit-per-cell.** The `PeriodicPusher` thread commits+pushes `results/` **once per newly-completed cell** (wakes every `PUSH_CHECK_INTERVAL`s, commits only when `run_count` increased) — one commit per result, each pushed immediately. `git_push_results` checks the push exit code and logs an explicit WARNING on failure instead of always printing "Pushed results".
315	- `generate_results.py` — generates `results.md` reports and updates `README.md`. Can run standalone: `python3 generate_results.py --all`. Each results.md opens with a "Claude Code versions used" line linking to the per-version docs (see `version_docs.py`).
316	- `combine_results.py` — produces cross-run combined reports `results/results_<dirA>__<dirB>[__<dirC>...].md`. Same table layout as per-run reports plus a CLI Version Legend; uses `judge_consistency_report.py` for the JCS section and `conclusions_report.py` for the Opus-max Conclusions prose. Standalone: `python3 combine_results.py <dirA> <dirB> [<dirC> ...]`.
317	- `recover_cost.py` — report-time-only floor recovery of a timed-out cell's spend from its partial `cli-output.json` event stream (SIGKILLed cells never emit the CLI's final cost record). Input/cache-read/cache-write tokens are exact per-message usage; output tokens are a conservative estimate from visible content plus thinking-token telemetry. Joins **Total Cost only** in `generate_results.py`/`combine_results.py` — never `geo_cost`/`geo_turns`, since a systematically-low floor would bias a ratio statistic.
318	- `monitor.py` — read-only **live** dashboard for an in-flight run. Groups completed cells by `variant` and prints per-variant run-health (duration, cost, turns, errors, actionlint, test-exec time), structural code metrics (impl files/lines, workflow files/lines, total lines — all non-LLM), structural test metrics (test files/lines, tests, assertions, assertions/test, test:code ratio — all non-LLM), and live-detected traps. The head-to-head is **automatic and always strongest-vs-strongest**: `strongest_model_short` (ranked by `model_power` — family, then version, then 1m>200k context) picks the most powerful model+version in *this* run and in the *previous report* (auto-detected: newest run with a `summary.json` older than this one), then matches them by task+language at each shared effort. It also breaks the comparison down **per scripting language** and flags languages whose deltas differ significantly (≥1.5σ and ≥25 pts) from the cross-language mean. Override the auto-pick with `--baseline DIR` (which prior run; `none` to skip) and/or `--pair RUNVAR=BASEVAR` (exact variant pairing); for full cross-model rollups use `combine_results.py` post-run. On Claude-subscription auth it also prints the **weekly subscription allowance** via `GET /api/oauth/usage` (the endpoint behind the CLI's `/usage`): five-hour + weekly limits from the `limits[]` array, annotating which weekly cap an Opus run draws from, plus `extra_usage`. It reads the OAuth token from `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, never logs it, degrades gracefully (skipped when there are no OAuth creds — e.g. API-key auth has no weekly cap — or on HTTP error), and can be disabled with `--no-usage`. `--total N` enables a pace-based ETA (a floor — later tranches run slower); `--watch SECS` refreshes. Pure logic (`aggregate`, `match_pairs`, `group_by_variant`, `model_power`, `strongest_model_short`, `flag_outliers`, `format_usage`) is unit-tested in `tests/test_monitor.py`; the `fetch_usage` network call and the structural/trap helpers (which reuse `test_quality.compute_structural_metrics` and `generate_results._detect_traps`) are best-effort and not unit-tested. Distinct from `watchdog.sh` (process supervision) and `generate_results.py` (post-run report).
319	- `test_quality.py` — test + deliverable quality evaluation. Structural metrics (always) + panel-of-judges LLM evaluation (`--llm-judge` for test-quality judge, `--deliverable-judge` for workflow+scripts judge). `compute_structural_metrics` returns `impl_lines`, `test_lines`, `workflow_lines`, and **`code_lines` = impl + test + workflow** (the authored-code total). The reports' Failed-Runs "Lines" column and the monitor's "total" now use `code_lines`, NOT the runner's `code_metrics.total_lines` (a whole-dir count that also includes fixtures, README, helper scripts, and the `act-result.txt` log). None of these line counts feed any quality score — those come from the LLM panel (which reads the code) + the structural test:code ratio (`test_lines/impl_lines`). The default panel is Haiku 4.5 + Gemini 3.1 Pro (configured in the module-level `JUDGES` dict). Each judge writes its own per-run cache file; `load_panel_scores(variant_dir, kind)` reads them and returns a mean-aggregated score dict for the reporting layer. Legacy single-Sonnet `*-llm.json` caches still read for backward compat. Imported by `generate_results.py` for the "Test Quality Evaluation" section.
320	- `llm_providers.py` — pluggable LLM provider abstraction for evaluation tasks (see "Adding LLM providers" below). Currently registered: `claude-cli` (pre-authenticated Claude Code CLI), `agy` (pre-authenticated Antigravity CLI — the Gemini path the `gemini31pro` judge uses; `agy -p` prints the response text directly, default model `Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)`), `gemini-api` (google-genai SDK, requires `GEMINI_API_KEY` and a paid-tier Google AI Studio account). The `gemini-cli` provider was **removed 2026-06-26** — per Google, *"On June 18, 2026, Gemini CLI and Gemini Code Assist IDE extensions will stop serving requests for Google AI Pro and Ultra, as well as those using it free of charge using Gemini Code Assist for individuals."* (https://developers.googleblog.com/an-important-update-transitioning-gemini-cli-to-antigravity-cli/); `agy` is its successor. See the removal note in `llm_providers.py`.
321	- `version_docs.py` — for each unique Claude Code version observed in a run dir's `metrics.json` files, writes `claude-code-<version>.md` with the full system prompt (concatenated from `Piebald-AI/claude-code-system-prompts` at tag `v<version>`), every default-tool description sorted alphabetically, and the slice of `anthropics/claude-code` `CHANGELOG.md` from the lowest CC version observed in any benchmark in this repo through that version. Standalone: `python3 version_docs.py [<run-dir>]`. Caches upstream content under `.cache/cc-versions/` (gitignored). Output files are referenced by name in each `results.md`'s prominent "Claude Code versions used" line.
322	- `benchmark-instructions-v*.md` — per-version specs given to agents during runs.
323	- `Dockerfile.act` — custom act container image with pwsh + Pester pre-installed. Build with `docker build -t act-ubuntu-pwsh:latest -f Dockerfile.act .`. Runner.py auto-detects it and injects `.actrc` into workspaces.
324	- `run-benchmark-web.sh` — provisioning + launcher for a **Claude Code on the web** cloud session (see "Running on Claude Code on the web"). Idempotent; `--setup-only` provisions without running. All other arguments pass through to `runner.py`.
325	- `run-fresh-matrix-*.sh` — per-campaign wrapper scripts that drive multiple sequential `runner.py` invocations (one per model-effort combo) into a single results dir using `--resume`. Use when the matrix needs more than one effort level; `runner.py` accepts a single `--effort` per invocation by design. See `run-fresh-matrix-2026-05-06.sh` for the canonical 8-invocation full-matrix template.
326	- `run-opus48-resume.sh` + `run-opus48-supervisor.sh` — the **resilient** per-campaign runner for the opus-4.8 (1M) campaign (run dir `2026-06-26_103905`; 7 tasks × 5 languages × 4 efforts medium/high/xhigh/ultracode = 140 cells). `run-opus48-resume.sh` runs all four tranches with `--resume` (re-runnable; skips valid cells). `run-opus48-supervisor.sh` is the entry point — launch via `setsid bash run-opus48-supervisor.sh` so it survives a session teardown; it restarts the resume worker whenever the runner dies, until all 140 cells are done. It takes an `flock` on `.supervisor.lock` (and `runner.py` on `.runner.lock`) so no two runners ever run concurrently. This pattern supersedes a plain one-shot launcher for multi-day runs that must survive crashes/reboots; pair it with `monitor.py` for live status (the supervisor and runner never need git for monitoring).
327	- `skills/` — agent skills following [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io/specification) spec.
328	
329	### Adding new trap detectors
330	
331	See the docstring on `_detect_traps()` in `generate_results.py`. Each trap needs:
332	a kebab-case name, detection logic over bash_cmds/console/metrics, a time estimate,
333	and an entry in `trap_applicable_mode` if mode-specific.
334	
335	### LLM vs structural discrepancy checks
336	
337	After every report generation (`python3 generate_results.py --all`), check the
338	"LLM vs Structural Discrepancies" section in each `results.md`. Discrepancies
339	are auto-classified by `_find_discrepancies()` in `generate_results.py`:
340	
341	- **counter-gap**: structural metrics are implausibly low (e.g. 0 tests or 0
342	  assertions while LLM scores high). This means `test_quality.py` is missing a
343	  test pattern. **Fix the counter** — read the generated test files to identify
344	  the pattern the counter doesn't recognize, add it to the appropriate
345	  `_count_*()` function and the detection/classification patterns, add unit
346	  tests, and regenerate. Counter-gap discrepancies should not persist across PRs.
347	- **qualitative**: structural metrics look reasonable but the LLM disagrees on
348	  quality. The report includes the LLM's justification (from the `summary`
349	  field in `test-quality-llm.json`). These are expected and acceptable — review
350	  the justification to confirm it's coherent, then leave them.
351	
352	If a **new counter-gap** appears after changing `test_quality.py`, it's a
353	regression. Fix it before merging.
354	
355	### Combined-report invariants (`combine_results.py`)
356	
357	The combined report (e.g. `results/results_<dirA>__<dirB>.md`) pools
358	runs across multiple source directories. A few layout invariants must
359	hold — changes here have broken the generated markdown before, so
360	`tests/test_combine_results.py` guards them:
361	
362	- **No duplicate `(language, variant_disp)` rows in Tiers or
363	  Comparison.** `aggregate_rows` groups by `(_disp_mode(language_mode),
364	  derived_label)` — `_disp_mode` collapses `powershell-tool` into
365	  `powershell` so the two pool into one column (#30; they are
366	  replicates in this WSL environment). `derived_label` is
367	  `<name-version>-<context>-<effort>` built by `_derived_label(m)`
368	  (name+version from `model_short` with the `-1m`/`-200k` suffix
369	  stripped and the legacy `opus`/`sonnet`→`opus46`/`sonnet46` rename;
370	  context from the **recorded** `contextWindow` in
371	  `model_usage_detail`, NOT the model_short suffix; effort from
372	  `effort_level` or, when null, `na` for Haiku / `high`-or-`medium`-
373	  by-CC-version for legacy Opus/Sonnet — see `derive_effort`). This
374	  grouping is injective per language mode, so the invariant still
375	  holds. CLI versions pool into one row; `cli_versions` retains the
376	  per-CLI breakdown for the legend. Because context comes from the
377	  recorded window, a mislabeled `opus47-200k` cell that actually ran
378	  at 1M pools into `opus47-1m-medium`, while genuine-200k `opus47`
379	  cells form a separate `opus47-200k-medium` row.
380	- **CLI Version Legend schema.** Exactly one CLI version per row.
381	  Columns: `Variant label | CLI version | Tasks | Languages`. `Tasks`
382	  and `Languages` each hold either `All` (pair covered every task /
383	  every language observed in the report) or a comma-sorted subset.
384	  The plural header `CLI version(s)` and comma-joined version cells
385	  are the old layout — do not reintroduce.
386	- **Section order in the body:** Scoring → Conclusions → **Judge
387	  Consistency Summary** → Tiers → Comparison → Per-Run → Notes. JCS
388	  is a top-level `##`, not a `### ` under Notes, because readers
389	  benefit from the panel-health verdict before they consume
390	  rankings.
391	- **Quality-score lookup key.** The per-variant score bucket is keyed
392	  by `(_disp_mode(language_mode), _derived_label(m))` — the display
393	  mode + CLI-less derived label, so quality-score pooling matches the
394	  duration/cost pooling in `aggregate_rows` exactly (including the
395	  `powershell` + `powershell-tool` collapse). Aggregate lookups therefore use
396	  `r["variant"]` (the derived label), NOT `r["variant_with_cli"]`.
397	  (Panel JSONs are still retrieved by the on-disk path
398	  `(source_run_dir, task_id, original_subdir)` where `original_subdir`
399	  comes from `_path_label` = RAW model_short + effort — retrieval is
400	  unaffected; only which aggregate row a score rolls up into changed.)
401	  Watch for the failure mode where a pooled row's Avg Tests Quality /
402	  Workflow Craft renders `—` or reflects only one context variant when
403	  it should be the mean across the whole derived-label pool.
404	
405	### Where the Conclusions prose lives
406	
407	The max-effort Opus `## Conclusions` block is produced **only for
408	the combined cross-run report** (`combine_results.py`), not for
409	per-run `results.md` files. `generate_results.py` still invokes the
410	JCS Summary LLM call (cheap) but passes `speed_cost_input=None` so
411	`conclusions_report.generate_conclusions_from_inputs` short-circuits
412	the Conclusions call. Reasoning: comparing a single run directory
413	against itself doesn't surface tradeoffs worth ~$1 of max-effort
414	tokens per regen — the Conclusions prose only reads as useful when
415	multiple run dirs are being compared.
416	
417	If you need per-run prose for some new purpose, plumb through a
418	separate prompt; do not re-enable the merged Conclusions call at the
419	single-run site.
420	
421	### Judge rationale audit (`judge_audit.py`)
422	
423	The combined report includes a `## Judge Audit Outcomes` section
424	that lists every run where the panel judges span ≥ 4 points on a
425	1–5 scale (i.e. Haiku = 1, Gemini = 5). For each flagged row the
426	audit scans each judge's rationale for concrete file-existence
427	claims (see `MISSING_PHRASES` + file-extension regex) and resolves
428	them against the run's `generated-code/` tree. Drop rule:
429	
430	- One judge contradicted → drop that judge's score; panel mean
431	  becomes the other judge's number.
432	- Both contradicted → drop both; panel mean becomes `—` and the
433	  row is excluded from aggregates.
434	- Neither contradicted → keep both.
435	
436	Verdicts persist as `judge-audit-<kind>.json` next to each run's
437	judge caches. `test_quality.load_panel_scores` consumes the verdict
438	automatically, so the Tiers / Comparison / LLM-as-Judge tables
439	above honor the audit with no extra plumbing.
440	
441	### Per-judge prompt addendums
442	
443	`JUDGES[...]` in `test_quality.py` accepts a `prompt_addendum_tests`
444	key. The test-quality evaluator appends it to the shared rubric for
445	that judge alone, so a model-specific steer (e.g. Haiku's
446	missing-file sanity note) doesn't drag the other judges along.
447	`python3 test_quality.py --rejudge haiku45 <run_dir>` refreshes
448	only that judge's cache — handy after tweaking its addendum.
449	
450	### Combined-report parity with per-run reports
451	
452	Per-run `results.md` carries three top-level sections the combined
453	report does not yet replicate in full:
454	
455	| Per-run section                  | Combined report status |
456	|----------------------------------|------------------------|
457	| `## Failed / Timed-Out Runs`     | Ported (2026-04-21)    |
458	| `## Test Quality Evaluation`     | Partial — structural metrics + panel LLM-as-Judge table ported; Correlation and LLM-vs-Structural Discrepancies sub-tables still absent |
459	| `## Savings Analysis` (Trap / Cache savings) | **Not yet ported.** Depends on per-run `_detect_traps` output + prompt-cache telemetry that aren't currently threaded into `combine_results.py`. Readers needing savings data should drop into the per-run `results.md` for now. |
460	
461	When porting the remaining bits, factor the section builders out of
462	`generate_results.py` into module-level helpers so both entry
463	points share a single implementation — the duplication we'd
464	otherwise accrue would drift the two reports out of sync.
465	
466	### Judge consistency summary (prompt hygiene)
467	
468	`JUDGE_CONSISTENCY_SUMMARY_SYSTEM_PROMPT` in
469	`judge_consistency_report.py` forbids unexplained shorthand. If you
470	surface disagreement rows, introduce them with the plain-language gap
471	size (e.g. "the widest disagreements — a judge scoring 1 vs 5, a
472	4-point gap on a 1–5 scale — include …"). Do not coin abbreviations
473	("Span-N", "Δ-N", etc.) that a reader has to decode. Cite specific
474	runs as `task-id-name / language / model-variant` (the same triple
475	the Per-Run table uses).
476	
477	Follow-up analyses of flagged disagreement rows live under
478	`results/analysis/` as dated standalone markdown files (e.g.
479	`judge_disagreement_1-vs-5_2026-04-21.md`). Link them from the JCS
480	section when regenerating if they remain relevant.
481	
482	### Updating model pricing
483	
484	Edit `models.py`. Check https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/models and
485	https://www.anthropic.com/pricing. Then run `python3 generate_results.py --all`.
486	
487	### Regenerating reports
488	
489	After changing `generate_results.py`, run:
490	```bash
491	python3 generate_results.py --all
492	```
493	This regenerates `results.md` for every run directory and updates `README.md`.
494	
495	### Adding LLM providers
496	
497	The LLM-as-judge evaluation in `test_quality.py` uses a pluggable provider
498	system defined in `llm_providers.py`. The benchmark runner (`runner.py`) is
499	inherently tied to the Claude Code CLI (it tests CLI-specific features), but
500	the evaluation layer is provider-agnostic.
501	
502	To add a new provider (e.g., Anthropic API, OpenAI, Codex CLI):
503	
504	1. Open `llm_providers.py` and create a class inheriting from `LLMProvider`.
505	2. Implement `is_available()` — return True when the provider can be used.
506	3. Implement `judge(system_prompt, user_message, model)` — return
507	   `{"text": str, "cost_usd": float, "input_tokens": int, "output_tokens": int}`.
508	4. Register it in the `PROVIDERS` dict at the bottom of the file.
509	5. Use it: `python3 test_quality.py --llm-judge --provider your-provider`.
510	
511	See the docstring in `llm_providers.py` for a complete example skeleton.
512	
513	## Before every PR
514	
515	1. **Run all unit tests and verify they pass:**
516	   ```bash
517	   python3 -m pytest tests/ -v
518	   ```
519	   All tests must pass. Do not create or update a PR with failing tests.
520	2. **If you added or changed code, add or update unit tests** in `tests/`.
521	   New functions need test coverage. Changed behavior needs updated assertions.
522	3. Run `python3 generate_results.py --all` and verify no errors.
523	4. **Check for counter-gap discrepancies** in the generated `results.md` files.
524	   If any "Probable counter gaps" appear, fix them in `test_quality.py` before
525	   merging (see "LLM vs structural discrepancy checks" above). Qualitative
526	   disagreements are expected — verify the LLM justification is coherent.
527	5. Verify all import paths work: `python3 -c "from runner import main"`.
528	6. Spot-check a few numbers in results.md against raw metrics.json.
529	7. If you changed architecture or findings, update this file (`AGENTS.md`).
530	8. If you added files or moved things, update the Files table in `README.md`.
531	
532	## Current state (2026-07-28)
533	
534	### Claude Code on the web — proved out, not a dataset (2026-07-28)
535	
536	`results/2026-07-28_114218/` was produced entirely inside a Claude Code on the
537	web cloud session via `run-benchmark-web.sh`: haiku45 × 2 tasks (11, 16) × the
538	standard 4 languages = 8 cells on CC 2.1.220. 8/8 succeeded, actionlint 8/8, an
539	`act-result.txt` in 8/8, 0 permission denials, $4.55 and 58.5 min of agent time.
540	It exists to prove the cloud path end to end — dockerd started by hand, act
541	executing workflows in the custom pwsh/Pester image through the egress proxy,
542	bun and pwsh cells passing, and the `--resume` loop skipping completed cells
543	(tasks 11 and 16 were two separate invocations into one run dir).
544	
545	Against the matched laptop cells in `results/2026-05-06_173435/` (same tasks,
546	languages and model) the aggregate is close — 58.5 min / $4.55 in the cloud vs
547	58.6 min / $4.25 on the laptop — but that comparison is confounded by CC version
548	(2.1.220 vs 2.1.131/132) on top of the environment, and n=8. It says "the cloud
549	sandbox is not obviously slower", nothing stronger.
550	
551	Treat it as infrastructure validation, **not** a dataset: one model, two tasks,
552	and the cloud tool surface described above. It is deliberately absent from the
553	README's Benchmark Runs table and "Latest results" pointer, which stay on the
554	last full campaign; regenerate them (`python3 generate_results.py --all`) only
555	when a real cloud campaign lands.
556	
557	### opus-4.8 (1M) campaign — COMPLETE; canonical dataset (2026-06)
558	
559	`results/2026-06-26_103905/` is the **canonical current dataset**: a complete v4
560	campaign adding `claude-opus-4-8[1m]` (model short `opus48-1m`) at four effort
561	levels — medium, high, xhigh, and the new **`ultracode`** (xhigh +
562	dynamic-workflow orchestration; enabled via `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=ultracode`,
563	since `--effort` does not accept it) — over the same 7 tasks × 5 languages = **140
564	cells** (136 successful; the 4 failures are xhigh PowerShell-family 30-min
565	timeouts: 12/powershell-tool, 13/powershell, 16/powershell-tool,
566	17/powershell-tool). CC versions: 2.1.193 (23 medium cells) + 2.1.195 (117).
567	Rate-limit clean (0 overloaded/rate-limit/529 markers). ~$578 cells + $17.25 panel
568	eval (Haiku via Claude CLI; Gemini 3.1 Pro (High) via `agy` = $0 on subscription).
569	Standard panel-of-judges scores populated; `results/CELLS-COMPLETE.md` marks
570	collection done. The cross-run report
571	`results/results_2026-06-26_103905__2026-05-06_173435__2026-04-17_004319__2026-04-09_152435.md`
572	pools opus-4.8 with the three prior runs and is the headline comparison artifact.
573	Note: opus-4.8 sometimes picks JavaScript / PowerShell for the free-choice
574	(default) language, not always Python.
575	
576	Headline findings (vs opus-4.7 1m, matched task+language): opus-4.8 is the
577	strongest generation on both quality axes (opus48-1m-ultracode tops Tests
578	Quality). It is +60–67% time / +64% cost at medium, compressing to ~+15% at high;
579	writes more and denser tests; the 4 xhigh failures are PowerShell-family timeouts.
580	**Trap caveat (see `results/analysis/opus48-trap-investigation_2026-06-28.md`):**
581	opus-4.8 logs ~2× the traps of 4.7, but a hand-review of all 201 occurrences found
582	this is ~99% benign (99% no circling, 86% legitimate iteration tripping count-based
583	detectors, ~1% genuine distress) — dominated by a `cd`-prefix dedup measurement
584	artifact + finer TDD, with a partial CC-version (2.1.131/132 vs 2.1.195) confounder.
585	Read "~2× traps" as "iterates more granularly," not "fails more often." Follow-up
586	work tracked in GH issues #21–#27.
587	
588	### v4 full-matrix benchmark — complete (now a baseline within the combined report)
589	
590	`results/2026-05-06_173435/`: 280/280 runs across 7 tasks × 5 modes × 8
591	model-effort combos, $493.46 + $40.57 panel eval = $534.03, 38h 35m wall, 278/280
592	successful (2 failures). Single-directory, single-CC-version-line (2.1.131 →
593	2.1.132 mid-run). It was the canonical dataset through 2026-06; it is now pooled
594	as the **opus-4.7 baseline** inside the opus-4.8 combined report above. Standard
595	panel-of-judges scores populated.
596	
597	The 8 model-effort combos: `haiku45` (no effort), `opus`/`sonnet` (no
598	effort), `opus47-1m` at high/medium/xhigh, `opus47-200k` at medium,
599	`sonnet46-1m` at medium. The 5 language modes: `default`, `bash`,
600	`powershell`, `powershell-tool`, `typescript-bun`. The 7 tasks: 11, 12,
601	13, 15, 16, 17, 18 (task 14 archived earlier).
602	
603	### Key findings vs prior baselines (CC 2.1.114 → 2.1.131/132)
604	
605	- haiku45 ~21% faster on average (driven by a bash-mode regression-fix
606	  on the haiku endpoint; bash specifically went 7× faster, while
607	  powershell got 33% slower).
608	- opus47-1m-high notably slower and pricier (+21% dur, +28% cost).
609	  opus47-1m-medium ~24% faster, opus47-1m-xhigh flat. Other variants
610	  within run-to-run noise.
611	- The earlier `2026-04-24_202012` partial run was abandoned (had
612	  widespread CLI-error failures on haiku/sonnet/opus variants — 46%
613	  failure rate). Stash dropped on 2026-05-08.
614	
615	### Earlier reference runs
616	
617	- `results/2026-04-17_004319/` — 245 runs, mix of `2.1.112` + `2.1.114`. Used as the haiku45 / opus47-1m / sonnet46-1m baseline.
618	- `results/2026-04-09_152435/` — 64/64, CC 2.1.97/98/100. Used as the no-effort opus / sonnet baseline.
619	- `results/2026-04-08_192624/` — v3, 64 runs, 1 timeout, 3 double-result bugs. Avg 11.4min/run.
620	- `results/2026-04-07_225702/` — v2, 111/144 runs. 18 tasks, modes: default/powershell/powershell-strict/csharp-script. Superseded by v3.
621	- `results/2026-04-02_163146/` — v1, 144 runs, same as v2. Had permission-denial artifacts (88% of errors).
622	- See `design-and-planning-artifacts/` for historical analysis and planning docs.
623	
624	### Per-CC-version reference docs
625	
626	Each run dir contains one `claude-code-<version>.md` per CC version
627	observed in its `metrics.json` files. Built by `version_docs.py` from
628	`Piebald-AI/claude-code-system-prompts` (system prompt + tool
629	descriptions at that tag) and `anthropics/claude-code` `CHANGELOG.md`
630	(sliced to [lowest CC version observed in any benchmark in this repo,
631	this version], oldest first). Each `results.md` links these
632	prominently in the "Claude Code versions used" line at the top.
633	
634	Regenerate after CC version changes:
635	```bash
636	python3 version_docs.py        # idempotent across all run dirs
637	```

# AGENTS.md

> **Managed by [`_agent-guidance`].**
> Edit only below the `## Repo-specific additions` header.
> Everything above it will be overwritten on the next sync.

## General guidelines

- Read existing code before modifying it. Understand the patterns already in use.
- Keep changes minimal and focused — fix what was asked, nothing more.
- Do not add speculative features, premature abstractions, or unused helpers.
- Prefer editing existing files over creating new ones.
- Never commit secrets, credentials, or .env files.

## Workstation layout

Repo locations are host-specific — match the convention of the machine you're on
(on Windows, check `$env:COMPUTERNAME`).

- **`ZENDA`** (Windows): local clones live under `D:\repos\<github-owner-or-org>\<repo>`
  (for example `D:\repos\adam-s-daniel\wsl-automation`). Clone new repos there, and
  assume existing repos live there rather than under the user profile
  (`C:\Users\<user>\...`).

## Code quality

- Follow the idioms and style already established in this repo.
- Write code that is clear enough to not need comments; add comments only when intent is non-obvious.
- Avoid introducing new dependencies unless strictly necessary.
- Every public interface change should include corresponding test updates.

## Security

- Validate all external input (user input, API responses, file contents).
- Never construct SQL, shell commands, or HTML by string concatenation with untrusted data.
- Use parameterized queries, shell arrays, and context-aware escaping respectively.
- Do not disable TLS verification, authentication, or CSRF protection.

## Data exposure in CI and public repos

Treat CI run logs, job summaries, artifacts, workflow run pages, and git history
as **public** on a public repo. (Real incident: a workflow printed the owner's
email addresses and their correspondents' into a public Actions log.)

- **Never print personal or sensitive data to a log** — no emails, contacts,
  names, IDs, mailbox sizes/counts, tokens, or anything "useful to an attacker or
  scammer." Deliver sensitive results out-of-band (e.g. email the account itself,
  write to a private store) and log only a non-identifying status line.
- **Don't interpolate `${{ inputs.* }}` / `${{ github.event.* }}` into a `run:`
  block** — the rendered command is echoed to the log. Read inputs from
  `$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` inside the script and `::add-mask::` sensitive values
  before use. `::add-mask::` only scrubs the log *stream*, not other surfaces.
- **Put sensitive config in secrets, not plaintext inputs or `vars`.** Only
  secret *values* are masked in logs.
- **Sanitize error output** — never dump an API/HTTP response body on failure (it
  can quote personal data); reduce it to a status code + machine error type, and
  keep the data-bearing serialization/call inside the try/catch.
- **Least privilege:** set `permissions:` to the minimum (usually
  `contents: read`) and require approval for outside-collaborator fork PRs.
- **Test fixtures use reserved `example.com` / `example.net` domains only** —
  never a real address; fixtures get committed and logged.

### git history & metadata
- **Sanitize before the first commit.** Fixing the current file does not remove
  data from history. If sensitive data was committed, rewrite history to drop the
  commits, delete every ref that points at them (branches, tags, **PRs**), and
  force-push. GitHub garbage-collects unreachable objects on its own schedule
  (days to weeks) — until then they remain reachable *by SHA* — and you can ask
  GitHub Support to expedite for a public repo. (This is the deliberate exception
  to "don't force-push"; it is a security remediation.)
- **Commit with the GitHub `…@users.noreply.github.com` identity** on public
  repos so a real email is not baked into commit author/committer metadata.

## Automation vs branch protection

Fleet repos enforce PR-only default branches via ruleset, managed as code in
`repo-settings` (see its ADR 0001). Design automation accordingly:

- Never design a bot that pushes to a protected default branch ad hoc — the
  push is rejected (GH013), even from the repo's own workflows.
- Generated data (badges, run summaries, reports, dashboards) belongs on a
  dedicated unprotected results branch (e.g. skills-evals' `eval-results`);
  consumers read from that branch and treat its content as untrusted.
- The rare bot that genuinely must write to a default branch needs a ruleset
  bypass actor declared in repo-settings' `fleet.yml` — never a hand-granted
  UI bypass (the drift report flags those). The AGENTS.md sync App is the
  standing example.
- PR + auto-merge is not a sanctioned bot-write path for fleet repos; the
  cms-platform-managed repos (outside the fleet ruleset) use it by their own
  design.

## Testing

- Run the existing test suite before considering a task complete.
- New behavior requires new tests; bug fixes require regression tests.
- Tests should be deterministic — no sleeping, no network calls, no reliance on wall-clock time.

## Subagent delegation (model routing)

- Don't write code in the main loop: run the implementation in a subagent on an
  appropriately lower-power model (e.g. the Agent tool's `model` override in
  Claude Code; skip if the harness has no subagent support).
- Route by mechanicalness: smallest model (haiku-class) for exactly-specified
  edits — pin bumps, renames, config/doc tweaks; mid-tier (sonnet-class) for
  normal implementation from a clear spec.
- The main loop keeps root-cause investigation, architectural decisions,
  writing the spec, and review of the subagent's diff before commit.
- Escalate the model rather than ship a wrong diff when the task is genuinely
  subtle (cross-repo invariants, race conditions).
- Don't assume the subagent sees this file: general-purpose and custom
  subagents receive the full memory hierarchy (imports included), but
  Explore/Plan-type agents and SDK harnesses with `settingSources: []` skip
  repo guidance entirely. Restate load-bearing constraints (style, test
  command, invariants) in the delegation prompt, and don't hand
  guidance-sensitive work to agents that won't see it.
- Give the subagent a precise spec — files, exact changes, house style, the
  test command to run. Subagent output is gated by the same test/CI proof as
  any other change.

## Skills ecosystem

- The canonical skills registry is `github.com/Adam-S-Daniel/agentskills`,
  organized as three bundle plugins — `adam` (general-purpose, cloud-safe;
  default-on), `adam-local` (machine-bound), and `fastmail` — each holding
  `skills/<skill>/` directories.
- In Claude Code with the marketplace installed, invoke a skill as
  `/adam:<skill>` (e.g. `/adam:pin-actions-to-sha`).
- Local machines get the marketplace plus per-agent symlinks via that repo's
  `setup.sh`.
- Cloud sessions currently get **no** plugins from repo-declared settings — a
  known Claude Code limitation (see agentskills' `docs/decisions/0001`) — so
  don't assume bundle skills are available there.
- New reusable skills graduate **into** the registry (sensitive ones into
  `agentskills-private`) rather than living on in a consumer repo.

## Git practices

- Write concise commit messages that explain *why*, not just *what*.
- One logical change per commit.
- Do not amend published commits or force-push shared branches.
